Proposal for the Appointment of Honorary Ambassador of the Just Do It Support Center Association  Dear Mr. Nicholas Marchesi,  It is with great honor that we present to you the proposal for granting you the title of Honorary Ambassador of the Just Do It Support Center Association. This title is awarded to individuals who, through their actions in supporting human rights, sustainable development, health protection, promoting diversity, and other areas aligned with our organization's mission, significantly contribute to the achievement of our goals. The title of Honorary Ambassador is given to social activists, politicians, philanthropists, and business leaders who have shown exceptional dedication to local and global communities.  About the Title of Honorary Ambassador:  The title of Honorary Ambassador is an honor that comes with great prestige and responsibility. Honorary Ambassadors serve a representative role, promoting the values and goals of the Association at the national and international levels. Those distinguished with this title engage in activities aimed at improving the quality of life, supporting sustainable development, and implementing the ideas of equality, education, and social integration.  Benefits of the Honorary Ambassador Title:  1. Representing the organization: The Honorary Ambassador becomes a representative of the Just Do It Support Center Association at prestigious conferences, international and national meetings, and participates in events organized by our organization.   2. Building leadership position: This title provides the ambassador with exceptional recognition in the international and national community, enabling them to establish collaborations with other organizations, governmental institutions, and the private sector.   3. Increasing visibility: Honorary Ambassadors gain access to platforms that promote their activities, both on social media and through publications and the press, significantly increasing their recognition.   4. Collaboration with international institutions: The title of Honorary Ambassador enables direct cooperation with the UN, governments, and other international organizations in achieving common goals such as sustainable development, human rights, health, and education.   5. Exclusive events: Honorary Ambassadors receive invitations to exceptional events, conferences, galas, meetings with political and business leaders, and the opportunity to organize their own initiatives.   6. Certificate and official recognition: Those awarded this title receive a certificate, which serves as a prestigious confirmation of their commitment and contributions to the Association.   7. Participation in shaping the Association's actions: Honorary Ambassadors have the opportunity to actively participate in creating new projects, initiatives, and strategies carried out by our organization, giving them a real impact on the communities in which we operate.    About the Just Do It Support Center Association:  The Just Do It Support Center Association was founded in 2022 and is one of the largest and most dynamic non-governmental organizations in Poland. Our activities span across Europe, with projects focused on the social and professional integration of refugees, support for marginalized individuals, and the promotion of equality and human rights.  So far, we have gathered over 81,000 supporting members and more than 5,000 volunteers actively engaged in our initiatives. We collaborate with many international organizations, including the UN, and with governments, implementing projects related to sustainable development, health protection, education, and combating disinformation.  One of our key activities is participation in the Global Digital Compact organized by the UN, which aims to build global cooperation in the areas of digital and social development. Additionally, we are carrying out projects such as the "Reliable Blogger" and "Crisis Volunteer," offering training on combating disinformation and providing support in crisis situations.  Our Association also helps in obtaining funding and grants for projects, offering support to organizations that strive to achieve similar social and humanitarian goals.  Summary:  Granting the title of Honorary Ambassador of the Just Do It Support Center Association is not only a prestigious distinction but also a real opportunity to influence social change, promote values of equality, human rights, and sustainable development. It is also an excellent opportunity for collaboration with global leaders, including international organizations, governments, and the business sector, in order to work towards a better future.  We invite you to accept the title of Honorary Ambassador of the Just Do It Support Center Association and to join us in working for justice, equality, and social integration.  Sincerely, Ivan-Oleksandr Yakymiv Vice President of the Board and Co-Founder Just Do It Support Center Association

Hi Nic,  Thanks for the chat last week, I’ve been considering our conversation and wanted to share my thoughts and insights on the OSA remote Indigenous program.  I see a wonderful opportunity for OSA to positively impact the health and well-being of people in remote communities through the implementation of the laundry service.  However, as you are learning there is much complexity and the underlying health issues stem from high levels of social, economic and environmental disadvantage, and cultural destruction.  Culture represents the heartbeat of these communities. It provides the context in which individuals and communities define themselves and defines what motives them to progress from physiological needs to self-actualisation (Maslow’s Hierarchy).  People need to see a relevant link between the program and how it supports their aspirations and builds culture. Programs/projects that focus only on a specific area have limited impact as opposed to those that work with communities to increase their capacity as a community and strengthen their overall cohesiveness and resilience.  The first step is to define the aspirations of the community, then map how the program, being a laundry, opshop etc supports these aspirations to come to reality. (see attached)  As an isolated service, the laundry answers some of the critical needs including health and hygiene, and a welcoming and supportive environment. The integration of the OpShop and the laundry as a ‘community-owed social enterprise’ provides a much broader opportunity, including a hub that acts as a safe space, capacity building activities and seed funding for new community-driven initiatives to spout.   By flipping the free service model currently in place to a community-owned enterprise you flip the paradigm of a hand-out mentality that creates dependence to a hand-up mentality that promotes agency and empowers the community to drive and determine their own future.   With this in mind, my proposal to OSA is as follows:  o Employment under OSA as the Head of Social Enterprise Development - Remote Indigenous Communities Stream  Responsible for leading social enterprise activities for OSA, with the focus on creating sustainable models that build social, cultural, economic and environmental capital in remote Indigenous Australian communities.   Key responsibilities include:  o Research, development and scaling up of social innovation programs o Development of an OSA Indigenous engagement framework o Development of an OSA ‘Remote Launch Pad’ program for community-owned social enterprise development (Integrated opportunity shop (OpShop) and laundry service) o Responsible for the establishment of new communities o Management and training of community facilitators (coordinators/volunteers) o Design and implementation of marketing and communication campaigns o Design and utilisation of performance metrics and impact measurement tools o Key stakeholder management (community/government/NGO/business etc) o Raising of startup and philanthropic resources to support emerging social enterprise projects   Immediate objectives of phase one would be to:  o Assess the current pilot project in FNQ and make adjustments where necessary to meet desired short to mid-term outcomes. o Facilitate community engagement in OSA laundry service on country - (7-10 days a month in the community - flexible depending on community cultural obligations / weekly calls) o Scoping the current needs and capacity of next tier communities   Once the OSA Laundry service has been refined, the integrated model (opshop/laundry) would be promoted as a partnered initiative. The OpShop or the Laundry may spin out as stand-alone initiatives depending on the needs of the community and or provide the foundation for other spin-offs.    The Remote OpShop Project (Remote Opportunities Australia) would be auspiced under OSA for an agreed period.   As my life is established in Northern NSW, I would be looking for a flexible working arrangement, where I could work from a home office with regular check-ins to HQ (zoom and in-person). This also provides respite as travelling and living on community can be an at times be an intensive experience.   I’ve attached a PDF that showcases the expected outcomes as they relate to Maslow's Hierarchy which gives insight into my theory of change.  As mentioned in our chat, this my blue-sky dream - I would love input from you on how I can further refine this and add value to the mission and vision of OSA.  Look forward to hearing from you,  Tanya

CONTENT: Hey Nicholas,  By way of introduction, my name is Melisa Sloan and I am a lawyer, board director and author. Please also find attached my bio which expands on my experience for your perusal.  The purpose for me reaching out to you is that I am currently writing my second book, “Big Moments, advice for conquering those big moments that define us.” It’s a book for 20-45 year olds as a guide to helping them conquer the big moments in their life – buying their first pad, starting their hustle, getting married, travelling, caring for parents,  making big financial decisions and so on.   Throughout my book I have reached out to some wonderful experts to provide their top tips which have been incorporated into the chapter relevant to their specific area of expertise.  I thought you would be a wonderful addition to my book as one of the experts in my “The End Game”  chapter (the name is only a working name and may change!). The chapter is intended to be an inspirational chapter, with some stories/ insights from some really inspirational people.   Having followed your journey from when you founded Orange Sky I have found you so inspirational, and a visionary in a world where we need many more people like you, I thought you would be perfect as one of my book experts. I believe my readers would definitely find value in what you have to share and will be inspired by you and your journey.  So in that connection, I would really love if you were interested in being part of my book and sharing your top 5 insights into how to live your best life, and if you are inclined touching on the sustainability and the importance of giving back.   Andrew Griffith’s is one of my contributing experts and he has kindly agreed to me sharing his contribution to my book to give you an insight to what I have in mind for each expert’s contribution to the book.   A copy of his contribution is attached. His contribution is just under five hundred words and that is all that I would expect from you. If you prefer , I am happy to chat with you by phone or have a zoom with you to discuss your top five insights and put it all on paper for your approval. With other experts this have involved an initial half hour chat, plus some time to review the finished copy that I subsequently forward to you. Let me know what works best for you and when would be an ideal time to have a chat.  All expert commentary will be showcased in my book and acknowledged, and you will have formal approval of the final draft submission in respect to your contribution, together with approving the final layout of your contribution. Hi Nicholas,  Thanks so much for replying so quickly!   I am about 20 min outside DC.  And you may know that apparently DC is the NFP hub.   Re your specific question. I don't have anything concrete yet - tbh. I have met a couple of people who work in the NFP space and I was planning to reach out to them and ask for advice/help with navigating funding, structure, processes, etc. and how fundraising works here and where to start. I also know someone who works in the IRS and another who was in finance at the White House, so I am planning to get their input around this too.  In Australia, I was involved in grant, tender and submission writing for government, corporate and private donors, and know it is a messy, time-consuming business.  With the contacts I have mentioned, I think I can get a rough outline of what to do and where to go here in Maryland.  To give you an idea of my approach and experience with grassroots funding/fundraising. My involvement was by necessity rather than due to my inherent skill! There was nobody working in this area and I became the accidental FR person. Luckily I'm not afraid to ask the questions - the worst that can happen is you get a 'no' - you've lost nothing by asking and you never know what might happen!  My approach is pretty direct - but friendly. Initially, I often ask for help or recommendations rather than for something concrete, and I also explain what I'm aiming to do. People often suggest people, organisations or approaches I'd never though of - which is great. I use these links and connections to arrive where I want to be and to build engagement in the process and for mission. As you know, if you bring people with you, you get more (even if not directly), as people become invested.  In a more structured scenario, I had contacts at KPMG in Australia and worked with some people in their social enterprise section to find ways of tapping into the particular type of cause for the relevant period - whether it was FY or a 3 year plan or whatever. I have also approached businesses, which might have some affinity for the cause to tap into any charitable approach they may have.   I understand that to scale something and to make it sustainable you need more than the grassroots or even corporate approach. Consistent funding from more than one source is needed, as is constant work to keep your organisation front of mind for funders - even those that may seem to lack any human input - such as government, to ensure your organisation remains relevant. This is where I hope my IRS, government and NFP people can help me.  I hope this information is helpful and enough to continue a conversation.  Thanks again for responding. Very much appreciated.  Terry

It talks a lot about logotherapy….  The notion of logotherapy was created with the Greek word logos ("meaning"). The concept developed by Frankl is based on the premise that the primary motivational force of an individual is to find a meaning in life. The following list of tenets represents basic principles of logotherapy:  📌Life has meaning under all circumstances, even the most miserable ones. 📌Our main motivation for living is our will to find meaning in life. 📌We have freedom to find meaning in what we do, and what we experience, or at least in the stance we take when faced with a situation of unchangeable suffering.

SUBJECT: Orange Sky
CONTENT: Hi Nic,  I am writing to introduce myself and say thanks for the great work you, Lucas and the Orange Sky team do. It is very much needed and the success of what you've achieved so far is well deserved. I can see that your work as usual is stopped because of COVID-19, but I love that your team is still looking for innovative solutions to these challenges - one thing I really love about Orange Sky.   I've also just had a look at some of the team in LinkedIn - young, dynamic, clearly driven individuals  - something I find refreshing and inspiring.   I recently saw your advertized role for a Fundraising Manager but did not apply as I'm living abroad. However, my circumstances have changed and I will be returning tp Australia later this year, so I wanted to connect with you & stay in touch, should you need someone with my skills once the COVID-19 situation is over.   My background is community development and my heart belongs in the community. I've worked all over the world - leading teams in Australia, Asia and the Americas. I've worked with vulnerable women and children, co-led the world's largest peace education program for children, 'The Peace Crane Project', been a selected guest speaker at the UN for my work in global peacebuilding and am a Rotary Global Grant Scholar. I have been responsible for all kinds of fundraising, for myself and the organizations I've worked with, for a total of more than $150K over time. I am also a communications specialist, priding myself on my ability to connect, engage and inspire people, businesses and organizations. I am proud of my ability to build and keep relationships also - you can check this through the references and friends I have maintained all every role I've had in my adult life (seriously, I can give you my bosses number at each job!). I also have a great personal network who I could leverage for fundraising for Orange Sky. This includes high net-worth individuals and businesses in Sydney and Brisbane.   I also noted in the application questions that you need to be adaptable and flexible for the wild ways of your organization. I actually wish I had the opportunity to laugh about this with you because, trust me, anything that gets thrown at me - I can handle it. I've lived and worked in Cambodia for four years, and really, it is a far stretch from the organized way of life in Australia. I've dealt with challenges on a daily basis, from gender and age discrimination, project mess ups and now leading communications for our 8 companies and 2000 local & international staff during a global pandemic. I am proud to be someone that focusses on solutions and maintains a positive outlook to get work done, no matter what. If a jobs got to get done, it's got to get done and I am proud that I am always able to think critically, work with my amazing team and achieve this.   I am telling you all of this because I feel like I'd be a really good fit for Orange Sky. I am working in an amazing role right now but am heading back to Aus and want to feel passionately about my job again. I love serving the community and I genuinely feel very strongly about what Orange Sky is doing, and I want to be a part of it.   I hope we can connect in some way, at some point later down the track - even if it's just to have a coffee once social distancing isn't a thing anymore. Would love to say hello and learn more about what you do - and, with a bit of luck, join your team and contribute to the great work Orange Sky does. I feel like once everything is back to normal the team will need to hit the ground running to get back to work, so I'd love to be there to be a part of that journey. I'm well experienced im start ups and am currently coping with COVID-19 here in Cambodia, so I'm sure I'd add value to making sure we pick up where we left of and getting back to normal, stronger than before.   Thanks so much for your time to read this and chat soon.  Sarah

Here goes ...   1) What (5 points on CM)   a) Community Mates’ aim: is to globally bring people, businesses and charities together and help provide access to discrete volunteering opportunities; and provide opportunity for people to volunteer with their friends thereby making volunteering an easy, fun and social activity.  These sorts of activities could support anything from social disadvantage, child cancer research, to animal welfare, to environmental causes, to efforts to assist the underprivileged etc etc. They are all important and they all make a difference!  Community Mates has provided a model for volunteering from school students to those beyond 80yrs who live in retirement homes – lifelong volunteering. b) Model, Operating Structure, & Budget: Operates on a completely decentralised volunteer basis. Founded in September of 2012, the entire organisation has operated on a budget of less than $5000 to date.   c) Charities Supported: over 200+ NFPs and Charities and has also previously acquired and integrated other charities. d) Hours: Has contributed over 20,000 volunteer hours e) Geography: has operated in seven countries and every state and territory in Australia  2) Why (5 points on why we think we should do this)   a) Mission – “to Positively Connect Communities”: This is absolutely on point with our mission! Furthermore it helps us give opportunities to the 10,000+ volunteers who have applied to volunteer with Orange Sky but who we weren’t able to give volunteering opportunities to. CM offers a structure and platform for us to be able to do just that. We already have the volunteer assets, this is a logical next step in us being able to use them and positively connect communities from school age students to those in retirement homes! Connecting communities is about lifelong volunteering. b) Values: Understanding the needs of volunteers, and finding new & more innovative ways to satisfy them, is something we are super passionate about and believe is the key to sustaining and scaling an organisation's social Impact. c) Strategically Aligned - Fundraising: Talk about Will’s thoughts on how donors would be further impressed by this initiative and that it could greatly benefit Orange Sky’s broader fundraising efforts d) Strategically Aligned – Campfire: Selling software products in competitive. CM provides us with an opportunity to build relationships with NFPs, charities, and businesses much faster and as a servant. From which we can then further expand those relationships by bringing Campfire to their attention. e) Reputationally Value Accretive for Orange Sky: M&A is common practice in the private sector as it drives efficiencies, increases scale, and helps create stronger organisations that make a greater impact. M&A within the third sector is however incredibly rare – almost unheard of – but provides a massive opportunity to help scarce fundraising $ go to those in need rather than administration. This opportunity to acquire CM at no cost gives Orange Sky another major point of differentiation against other charities as an innovator, leader, and inspiration in the sector. Each being the key underpinning for further expanding our relationship with donors and government.    3) How / When (what do we need to do / next steps)  a) NM & LP seek board approval to work toward proposal b) NM & LP to work with Community Mates to formulate a proposal c) NM & LP present proposal for Board approval d) Upon Board approval - complete the acquisition e) Integrate CM as a division of Orange Sky - On another note, if we can come to landing and get board approval, I have a good mate in Brisbane who I might possibly be able to pull a favour from, who could help you guys integrate CM into Orange Sky for no cost. He’s an ex top tier strategy consultant, Masters from Oxford, MBA from UQ, and has done a heap with CM so his expertise would be invaluable in working out the integration details and operational mechanics etc.

I'm Amelia St Baker, JCI Brisbane Director of Partnership, and I'm contacting you as I would like to know if you're interested to be nominated for an award that has been won in the past by Daniel Flynn (Founder of Thank You water), The Oaktree Foundation Founder and Global Citizen CEO, Hugh Evans, and Zambrero Owner and CEO, Dr. Sam Price.  The award is called the TOYP (Ten Outstanding Young Persons) and is presented by JCI Australia. I will explain it in more detail below:  What is JCI?  Junior Chamber International, commonly referred to as JCI, is a non-profit international non-governmental organization of young people between 18 and 40 years old for young people to develop leadership skills, meet inspiring people and make a real impact in local communities. It has members in about 124 countries, and regional or national organizations in most of them and count over 200,000 members.  The first local Junior Chamber chapter was founded in 1915, but the international umbrella organization Junior Chamber International (JCI) was founded in Mexico in 1944. It has consultative status with the Council of Europe, with the Economic and Social Council of the United Nations and with UNESCO. It encourages young people to become active citizens and to participate in efforts towards social and economic development, and international cooperation, good-will and understanding.  What is the TOYP?  JCI Australia seeks nominations of exemplary young active citizens from across the country in all fields of service, with honourees recognised at the JCI Australia National Convention. The National Convention this year will be hosted by our chapter in Brisbane this year! National honourees will have an opportunity to represent JCI Australia in the global TOYP Program. Each year JCI serves to formally recognise young people who excel in their chosen fields and create positive change through the TOYP Program. By recognising these young people, JCI raises the status of socially responsible leaders in this world. The honourees motivate their peers to seek excellence and serve others. Their stories of discovery, determination and ingenuity inspire young people to be better leaders and create better societies.  Since 1983, JCI has honoured nearly 300 individuals from 57 nations. Past recipients of national awards include such well-known personalities as John F. Kennedy, Henry Kissinger, Elvis Presley, Jackie Chan, Wayne Gretzky and many more, all named before the age of 40 and before they had achieved national prominence. Honourees selected in past years have represented the heights of progress in numerous human endeavours. Many have gone on to even greater achievements. All have continued to serve humanity in a great variety of ways.  If successfully selected by the international program as a TOYP honouree, Australian honourees will be sponsored by JCI to travel to the 2020 World Congress in Yokohama, Japan from November 3-7 to attend the formal awards ceremony. This includes complimentary registration to World Congress, with flights and accommodation included.   What's next?  Let me know if you're interested in being nominated for the TOYP and we can set up a meeting to go further in details in person.   Looking forward to hearing from you.  Regards Amelia St Baker

SUBJECT: Panel event at University of Melbourne
CONTENT: Hi Nicholas,  I’m the program manager at GSA, the University of Melbourne’s graduate student association. We are a growing organisation and particularly this year have been making some great strides in representing and serving graduate students.  In the next few months we are working on a great program, called GSA LEAD (Leadership Exploration and Development), and organising an event on November 20 which I think would greatly benefit from your background and expertise in Orange Sky Australia.  There is a great buzz around our new pilot program - you can see our participants (called Explorers) who attended a retreat last weekend to kick off the program. The program is seeking to promote individual leadership growth and using the social change model, promote ways of changing the world in socially responsible ways.  On November 20, from 6pm – 9pm, at the University of Melbourne we want to deliver to our 35 Explorers and Hosts a panel of leaders who have been involved in socially responsible enterprises or endeavors. We think you speaking to you or Lucas (or both of you) speaking to your work at Orange Sky Australia would be a fantastic contribution to the program. We’re looking at 3-4 other panelists, potentially Kon Karapanagiotidis from the Asylum Seeker Resource Centre, Michelle Evans who has worked supporting indigenous enterprise, and others.   More info on the program here: https://gsa.unimelb.edu.au/work-skills/lead-leadership-exploration-development/  I’d love a chance to chat with you further about this opportunity to promote your work and inspire graduate students. Feel free to call or email me back anytime (contact details below).  Beornn McCarthy Program Manager University of Melbourne Graduate Student Association   1888 Building | The University of Melbourne | Parkville Vic 3010 e: beornn@gsa.unimelb.edu.au | m: 0401 626 563 | p: 03 8344 8380  We acknowledge the Wurundjeri People as the traditional custodians of the land.

SUBJECT: Chat to understand homelessness
CONTENT: Hi Nick, I'm a new volunteer at Orange sky, starting my orangetation next Wednesday. I've been following what your team have been doing for a few years now and love what you do for people in need.  I am part of team in a NFP startup looking at tackling a different side issue of homelessness - how people without a home receive support in a cashless society.  We are looking to talk to people who understand the problem at heart and were wandering if someone in your team would be available for a chat to help us understand the problem more thoroughly, and understand how our platform may be of use to people experiences homelessness.  As we all know, homelessness is a complex issue with no single solution, so we are in need of help to understand the current landscape so that our service can offer the right assistance.  A catchup over the phone or over lunch would be amazing (based in Syd though).  Look forward to hearing from you.  Best regards,  Sam

As Youth Ambassador for Chloe’s Law/Voice, as the Hills Shire Youth Ambassador, I am standing up and putting up my hand. Bullying is not ok.  The 12th September 2014 means its been 12 months since we lost Chloe to bullying.  Chloe’s story received national attention 12 months ago – what has happened since…  It’s been 12 months of work to bring about change to our anti-bullying laws. 49,000+ name petition, signed by people across Australia, calling on the Government to enact strong anti-bullying laws was delivered to Tasmanian Senator Eric Abetz on 6th September 2014.  Senator Abetz will presenting the petition to Parliament on 22nd September 2014.  As Chloe’s Law/Voice Youth Ambassador, as Hills Shire Youth Ambassador, as an 18-year-old girl, I am passionate about raising awareness of anti-bullying in our country.  You may remember Chloe's Law/Voice is an anti-bullying campaign about a young girl, Chloe Ferguson, who took her own life after being bullied for years - the final straw, being physically bashed after getting off a bus after school and cyber-bulling – all because she didn't have a mother.  We can not let anyone ever feel so helpless again.  Please share “SAY NO TO BULLYING DAY” - raise awareness and spread the message of anti-bullying.  Our slogan "STAND UP. BE STRONG" is about working together to make a difference. With over 289,000 likes on Facebook, our country is “STANDING UP”!  Australians want an end to bullying.  According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, 23, 745 students surveyed in 2013 stated that their biggest social and environmental concern is reducing bullying in school in every state in Australia.  Together, let’s change these statistics.  Our anti-bullying anthem “Be Strong” is raising awareness, striking a cord within our community.  “Be Strong” acknowledges pain, encourages strength and moving on.  Please help share our anti-bullying message and our anti-bullying anthem "Be Strong": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0tSDBZByww0   I honestly believe that together we can make a difference.  What else can you do?  Other than sharing our anti-bullying anthem, “Say No to Bullying Day” is a day to raise awareness and educate on the devastating effects that bullying has on the community.  The plan is to wear blue and/or change your profile/cover photo on Facebook to Chloe's Law for the day to show support!  You can even register with Chloe’s Law/voice which is a nationaly registered non-for-profit organisation, to host an event - morning tea or afternoon tea, etc.  All funds raised will be donated to Chloe's Law/voice to allow them to continue to make a difference by offering awareness, educational speaking, guest speaking, advocacy programs and support across Australia. The series, which launched last month, comprises 14 hourlong lectures, including live Q&As with the speakers. Whether this is your first conversation around race and technology or one of many, be prepared to understand the field in a new way.
